sources.title: United States Office of the Historian, Armenia: recognition and diplomatic history
sources.note: Directly read, especially summary and recognition in 1920. Distinguishes actual First Republic from proposed boundaries; Soviet invasion, Transcaucasian federation and 1936 union-republic status.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, World War I and the Armenian Genocide
sources.note: Directly read conflict-zone discussion. Used only for Ottoman/Russian wartime setting; no disputed population percentages or erroneous modern Turkish proclamation date reproduced.

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, The Armenian Genocide, 1915 to 1916: overview
sources.note: Directly read. Public passage clearly identifies deliberate destruction of Ottoman Armenian communities and displacement without graphic description.

sources.title: National Assembly of Armenia, Women MPs of the First Republic (7 April 2021)
sources.note: Original parliamentary retrospective checked through indexed text. Three of eighty elected in 1919; Katarine Zalyan-Manukyan’s Medical-Sanitary Commission work and Varvara Sahakyan’s refugee relief. Avoids celebratory claims of universal equality.

sources.title: Yerevan State University Museum, The foundation of Yerevan State University
sources.note: Directly read. Law 16 May 1919; temporary opening Alexandropol 31 January 1920; one-day newspaper, student assistance fund. Counted with Armenian version as one work.

sources.title: Yerevan State University Museum, Երևանի պետական համալսարանի հիմնադրումը
sources.note: Direct Armenian text read, section «Հայաստանի համալսարան» թերթը. Exact motto «Գիտութիւնն ոյժ է» of 31 January 1920 newspaper; English version renders Science is power. Published transcription, not fresh reading of image.

sources.title: Yerevan State University, Historical reference to its 101st anniversary, part 2 (24 April 2020)
sources.note: Directly read institutional history: textbook translation from 1922, imported equipment and Leon Orbeli’s 1926 purchases.

sources.title: Near East Relief Historical Society, Mass Entertainment: Toys and Games in Near East Relief Orphanages (2018)
sources.note: Full text and captions read. Alexandropol-specific gymnastics circa 1920, gardens and mud houses, outdoor music lesson of uncertain date. Sidon and Beirut examples are not transferred to Armenia.

sources.title: Near East Relief Historical Society, Citizen Philanthropy: Say It With Flour! (2019)
sources.note: Directly read sections on 1921 flour collections and orphanage bread. Explicitly says bread type unknown; modern matnakash recipe is not historical proof. Introductory erroneous 1917 end-of-war date is not used.

sources.title: Erich Kettenhofen, George Bournoutian and Robert Hewsen, Erevan ,  Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Directly read modern-history section: Tamanyan 1924 plan, boulevards, 1930s electricity, sewers and water, removal of older structures. No claim that all households had service.

sources.title: Yerevan State University, Kamsar Arakelyan, rector 1937 to 1938
sources.note: Original university Russian biography indexed text verified: arrest 8 January 1938, later imprisonment/exile, rehabilitation in 1955 for lack of an offense. English URL unavailable; Russian original used.
